expectedLearning: Whether a plain descriptor-driven TypeScript facade can remove low-level identity and storage boilerplate while retaining exact domain value types and the existing identity laws.
Whether explicit derived dependencies and dependency-version fingerprints provide lazy selective recomputation without runtime read tracking or semantic-history side effects.
Whether a supply-tax pressure exemplar, fixed LLM-shaped corpus, and representative graph scale probe justify the facade boundary without public promotion.
allowedWork: Internal typed state descriptors, handles, transaction compilation, derived graph, evaluator, cache, diagnostics, tests, measurements, one typed supply-tax exemplar, and supporting documentation.
Narrow changes to the existing semantic-state kernel and one-way authority adapter required by named operations.
disallowedWork: No runtime Proxy authority, implicit assignment, generic stage exposure, public facade, global registry, filesystem code generation, renderer, animation, timeline, interpolation, Article, or browser work.
No economics authority fork, broad domain pack, storage redesign, CAS, theorem prover, knowledge or procedure system, macro catalogue, or live LLM integration.
